blocks.text: A **slice** (`[]T`) is a view of flexible length over an array (or a block of memory). If a function parameter is `[]i32` it accepts an array of any size. For a sub-range write `array[a..b]` (`b` not included).
A slice is a view, so the array it is made from cannot change, move or disappear while the slice is in use. The compiler checks this, so a slice can never "dangle".

blocks.prompt: Write `average(items: []i32) -> i32`: the sum of the elements divided by their count (`items.len` is a `usize`, convert with `i32(items.len)`). Print it for `[2, 4, 6, 8]`.
blocks.hint: First find the total, then divide by `i32(items.len)`.

blocks.q: Which can be passed to a `[]i32` parameter?
options: A `[N]i32` array of any size, or a sub-range
blocks.why: A slice does not fix the length, so it works with any size.
